div.h1: Google Sheets Sync — rev 2 (newest-first display, append-only storage)

div.p: The IT team's sheet shows newest-first, meaning each new ticket is inserted at the top and every row below shifts down by one. A stored row index is therefore stale the moment the next ticket is encoded — a retry or a status update would silently write to the wrong ticket's row. That is data corruption, not a cosmetic bug.

Splitting the sheet fixes it at the root: the worker only ever appends to _raw, so row N is row N forever, and the Tickets tab reproduces the newest-first order the team already expects via a QUERY formula. Nobody has to change how they read the sheet.

Trade-off to raise with the IT team before building this: a QUERY output range is computed, so the Tickets tab becomes read-only. If they currently type remarks straight into the sheet, that workflow moves into the app. This is arguably a feature — it is what "the database is the system of record" actually means in practice — but it is a real change to their day and should not arrive as a surprise.

If they must keep hand-editing that tab, the fallback is to insert at index 1 with InsertDimensionRequest and pin identity to each row with Sheets developer metadata, which survives row shifts. More API calls, more moving parts, same correctness. Do not fall back to storing a bare row index.

ul.li: One-way sync only (DB → Sheet). Bidirectional editing creates write conflicts the SRS has no rule to resolve. Protect _raw so only the service account can write it.
Idempotency — row_key (the ticket_no) identifies the row, so a retried job updates rather than duplicating.
Rate limits — ~60 write requests/minute/user. Batch 100 rows into one call, especially during the historical backfill.
Denormalization happens at the boundary, not in the DB. IDs stay in Postgres; names are resolved only when projecting the sheet row.
Google Cloud Console setup: enable the Sheets API → create a service account → download the JSON key → share the spreadsheet with the service account's email as Editor.

text.tspan: order by A desc, B desc", 0)
→ newest at the top, as today
